newsitem.title: USA: Chevron agrees Kazakh oil line deal - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Chevron agrees Kazakh oil line deal - NYT.

text.p: Chevron Corp and other big oil companies have reached an agreement with the governments of Russia, Kazakhstan and Oman to build a $1.5 billion pipeline, the New York Times reported on Tuesday.
The newspaper cited the manager of media relations for Chevron as saying the companies and the governments had finished negotiations last week in Moscow.
The manager, Mike Libbey, said they were set to sign a final agreement on December 6.
Construction of the pipeline will begin next year and end in two years, he said.
The pipeline will link the Tengiz oil fields on the Caspian Sea in Kazakhstan and Russia's Black Sea port of Novorossiisk.
The newspaper said Chevron, which pumps 120,000 barrels from the oil fields, hopes to eventually ship 700,000 barrels a day.
It said Chevron and its partner Mobil could spend $20 billion during the 40-year life of the project.
Lukoil, Rosneft, AGIP SpA of ENI SpA, British Gas Plc and Oryx Energy Co are also participating in the project, the newspaper said.
